business_problem: Rockwell needed to reduce the time and inconsistency involved in diagnosing machine faults, preserve retiring workers' tacit shop-floor knowledge, and shorten training time for new technicians supporting hundreds of machines.
solution_summary: Rockwell Automation built its GenAI-Powered Maintenance Copilot on Microsoft Azure for the Singapore plant to turn hard-to-find troubleshooting knowledge into real-time guidance on the factory floor. The implementation draws on three explicit sources: veteran engineers’ expert know-how, data from Rockwell’s manufacturing software, and machine instruction manuals. Rockwell organizes this material in a database by symptom, cause and reaction. When a technician submits a natural-language question, Azure AI Search retrieves the most relevant prior fixes and manual passages, and Azure OpenAI Service in Microsoft Foundry uses GPT-5.4-mini to generate a step-by-step diagnosis and recommended actions. The copilot is served to workers on tablets and smart augmented reality goggles, while Azure security, identity and governance services provide enterprise protection and compliance. Microsoft Azure’s cloud-native architecture also supports scaling the design from one factory to deployments in Ohio, Poland and Mexico.
